title: free websites?
author: These_Western
selftext:
is there any free game making app i can use? one that requires manual publishing (so i can publish it on google store)

i dont mind of it has cooldowns or the sort. just need it to be free completely. i dont mind royalties either.

im sick of putting in prompts for 2 - 3 hours then it disappears because i need to pay in usd which is impossible for me.

comments.author: Constant_Physics8504
comments.body: Not really, AI has, on purpose, been distributed by multiple companies as a For Profit model. While they tout that they’re charging to pay for energy usage and workers, they are easily making bank. If you really want to do what you’re trying, you have 2 options. 1) Pay a subscription or 2) Buy a computer with an amazin gpu and get rigging/running, and use local LLMs

comments.author: TaylorCooper337
comments.body: Game engines are literally game making apps. Godot is a good one.

replies.author: These_Western
replies.body:
theyre complicated, like using blender. theres millions of buttons, and even if i press them i dont know what it does.

and i cant code so.

replies.author: TaylorCooper337
replies.body: gamedev is hard man. AI makes it much easier you don't have to know how to code but you will need to learn a game engine if you want to succeed. It takes hours to learn but a few youtube tutorials will get you going. I probably watched the same youtube tutorial on how to make a basic RPG in godot at least 100 times and rewrote the code from scratch each time before it "clicked". It's worth it though I promise. Pick an engine and stick to it. Godot is beginner friendly ans has lots of resources.

replies.author: These_Western
replies.body:
they dont tell you what is what. they just tell you to go here and here to do this
then you get this so you do this.

its frustrating to me. i want to learn but no one teaches me.

its like going to blender, they already expect you to understand the shortcuts. (though that is arguably understandable)

replies.author: TaylorCooper337
replies.body: You have to learn some stuff to be able to do stuff that's with anything man. And like I said there ARE tons of tutorials you can watch that will get you going quickly. There are just a few concepts you need to understand: Scenes, Scripts, and Nodes will get you started. These are concepts that will apply to every single game engine you go to use. Here is a small video [How To Start Making Games With Godot 4!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k340oCBXW-0)

replies.author: TaylorCooper337
replies.body: just want to add if you are using chatgpt desktop app you can literally make a new project, leave it empty, and add the file system as a project in chatgpt. Then go from there with your prompting and it will work on the files in the godot folder and bam you have your work in a project that persists.

comments.author: Gugadin_
comments.body:
gamecollab.io

you can describe the game in your natural language, then click on generate prototype. You will have enough credits per month to generate 1 or 2 builds.

you will have your game. the more details you add in the project, the better the prototypes will be. 

once you have money for AI agents like cursor and claude, you can use GameCollab MCP to polish the game.
